{"type":"text","timestamp":1794725857486,"sessionID":"ses_e2224ef0bffeU8KAfRDPYlBEa7","part":{"id":"prt_1ddff3e75001IVGxKjWAkgSijw","messageID":"msg_1ddfeea2c001RSJAWo414V0uAq","sessionID":"ses_e2224ef0bffeU8KAfRDPYlBEa7","type":"text","text":"Accused **`e34` (Jussi Koskinen, Finance controller)** on Day 20 with **>99.2% posterior probability**.\n\n### Key Evidence\n1. **Decoy Identified**: Message search on Days 1–2 identified `e24` (Emma Koskinen) as the angry decoy receiving ~50% of framed after-hours accesses (`P(e24) = 0`).\n2. **Recipient Intersection**: Leaked regular documents (`d1-2`, `d8-3`, `d11-1`, `d12-4`, `d15-1`, `d18-2`) deterministically narrowed suspects to the 10 Finance employees, and `c17` further narrowed recipients to `{e01, e05, e21, e23, e34}`.\n3. **Orthogonal Padded Canaries**:\n   - `c14-2` leaked with variant **`v2`** (`{e01, e05, e23, e34}`).\n   - `c17` leaked with variant **`v2`**, in which **`e34` was the sole non-innocent suspect** (padded with known-innocent employees from outside Finance).\n4. **Access Logs & Interviews**: `e34` accumulated 6 after-hours accesses vs only 12 daytime accesses (`33.3%` after-hours, matching the mole's `30%` rate) plus multiple evasive interview responses.","time":{"start":1794725854837,"end":1794725857482}}}
